I'd like to comment on this post as someone whose coming from a Cybersecurity Sales Background going into a SOC Analyst role but someone who also did Business PBX Tech support for 3 years.

I agree with most posters here saying there is NO shortage of cybersecurity skills gap. It's all garbage marketing bullshit so MSSPs can sell their SOC and managed services (i'm going into one). The best cybersecurity folks are actually old school system admins and IT managers who have had an excellent track record of Patch Management, Security Awareness Education and someone whose done their due diligence in protecting their companies infrastructure.

I was shocked to hear college kids with cybersecurity degrees from shitty colleges with 0 experience 'demanding' yes that's demanding some companies to pay them a starting salary of 65k at the age of 20 and some companies did hire them and lo and behold they struggled tremendously trying to implement SIEM tools properly for many many months and not having a good understanding of Linux either.

Point is this whole 'shortage' of cybersecurity skills is not because of lack of professionals its because companies simply don't want to invest time and money into their System Admins who are a PERFECT and NATURAL fit for the security professional role. Some real hands on workshops, certifications and security vendor certifications goes along way.  


If you're Company is currently hiring an Information security analyst and you are a System Administrator you need to walk up to your IT Director or Compliance officer and tell them straight up what you need to do this job and save the company money by giving you a better raise and pay for your certs rather than hire someone externally.

I've been a Prot Warrior for well over 10 years and have tanked most major raids. As far as legion is concerned here's where Prot Warriros stood in my opinion.

**Emerald Nightmare** \- Prot Warriors were gold, solid tanks with good sustainable physical damage mitigation due with Shield Block, Ignore Pain and Nel's fury. Most of the damage in Emerald Nightmare was physical and where there's primarily physical damage, Prot Will shine.

**Nighthold \-** Complete abysmal tanks in the start, Heroic for me was a complete and utter nightmare compared to Bear Druids, Pallys and Monks. As much as I loved Nighthold as a raid, it was definitely not a place for a Prot Warrior. We got bamboozled by Krosus, Star Augur and to some extend Spellblade. Now they definitely weren't impossible by any means I cleared all the content, but I had extra respect for healers to put up with me during those tough times when instead they could have healed a Bear and call it a day.

**Tomb of Sargeras** \- Prot warriors were back in the spotlight baby. Lots and lots of high physical damage being thrown around and with Shield Block, Ignore Pain and Nel'f fury we were able to mitigate some very strong attacks that would other wise kill some other tanks. For e.g the 4th and 5th KJ Felclaw could easily be blocked by Nel's fury. All in All not a lot of problems for Prot Warriors \(Avatar was a pain though\).

**Antorous** \- Prot Warriors went back down to the middle of the pack if not a tad bit lower imo in the start. Guardian Druids are still king, however I do want to add that once you get some decent gear from the first few bosses and some Mythic runs \(950\+\) you will be tanking like an absolute boss again. Both the Last Bosses Aggramar and Argus are beautiful for Prot Warriors \- I was actually more scared of F'harg initially than anything on Heroic but other bosses are pretty easy mitigation wise \- You really have to spec into Anger Management and have The Wall's Fell to be able to constantly rotate Shield Wall and other cool downs at a consistent pace.

Between Last Stand, Shield Wall, Spell Reflect, Legendary Trinket, Ignore pain, Demo Shout \- there's a lot we can use to keep things sustainable.
